decision_conditions: The applicant has failed to provide accurate and consistent plans showing the development as built and its relationship to the host dwelling. Insufficient information has also been submitted to satisfactorily demonstrate the lawful use and function of the outbuildings within the site. As such, the Local Planning Authority is unable to fully assess the proposal and its impacts. The proposal is therefore contrary to the requirements of Policies DMHB 11 and DMHD 1 of the Hillingdon Local Plan: Part Two - Development Management Policies (2020).

The proposed development, by reason of the design, siting, scale, extent and cumulative footprint of the three outbuildings, would result in the majority of the rear garden being occupied by built form, constituting an overdevelopment of the site. The proposal would be out of keeping with the established pattern of development in the surrounding area, where for the majority of properties rear garden spaces remain reasonably open, and would result in the loss of openness and spaciousness that contribute positively to the character and appearance of the area. Consequently, the development would appear visually intrusive and incongruous within the street, causing unacceptable harm to the character and appearance of the area.  The proposal is therefore contrary to Policies DMHD 1 and DMHB 11 of the Hillingdon Local Plan: Part Two - Development Management Policies (2020).

The proposed development, through the provision and retention of three outbuildings occupying the majority of the rear curtilage, would leave an inadequate level of private amenity space for the occupiers of the main dwelling, resulting in a poor standard of residential amenity. In addition, the use of at least two of the outbuildings as independent self-contained residential units would provide substandard living accommodation, lacking adequate internal and external amenity provision commensurate with the reasonable living conditions of residential occupiers. As such, the development fails to secure a satisfactory standard of living accommodation and residential environment and is contrary to Policies DMHD 16 and DMHB 18 of the Hillingdon Local Plan: Part Two - Development Management Policies (2020).

The proposed development, by reason of the provision and use of three outbuildings within the rear garden, including the use of at least two of the outbuildings as independent residential accommodation and/or for purposes capable of generating commercial activity, would result in an intensification of activity at the site. The increased level of occupation, associated noise and disturbance, additional comings and goings, and activity throughout the day and evening would result in an unacceptable impact on the living conditions of neighbouring occupiers. The proposal would therefore give rise to undue noise, disturbance and loss of residential amenity detrimental to the occupiers of adjoining and nearby properties, contrary to Policies DMHD 1 and DMHB 11 of the Hillingdon Local Plan: Part Two - Development Management Policies (2020).

The decision to REFUSE planning permission has been taken having regard to all relevant planning legislation, regulations, guidance, circulars and Council policies, including The Human Rights Act (1998) (HRA 1998) which makes it unlawful for the Council to act incompatibly with Convention rights, specifically Article 6 (right to a fair hearing); Article 8 (right to respect for private and family life); Article 1 of the First Protocol (protection of property) and Article 14 (prohibition of discrimination).

The decision to REFUSE planning permission has been taken having regard to the policies and proposals in the Hillingdon Local Plan Part 1 (2012) and Part 2 (2020) set out below, including Supplementary Planning Guidance, and to all relevant material considerations, including The London Plan - The Spatial Development Strategy for London consolidated with alterations since 2011 (2016) and national guidance.

In dealing with the application the Council has implemented the requirement in the National Planning Policy Framework to work with the applicant in a positive and proactive way. We have made available detailed advice in the form of our statutory policies from the  Local Plan Part 1, Local Plan Part 2, Supplementary Planning Documents, Planning Briefs and other informal written guidance, as well as offering a full pre-application advice service.

In order to ensure that the applicant has been given every opportunity to submit an application which is likely to be considered favourably. In addition further guidance was offered to the applicant by the case officer during the processing of the application to identify the amendments to address those elements of the scheme considered unacceptable which the applicant chose not to implement.
description: Erection of outbuildings to rear garden (Retrospective planning application).
